items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1962-02-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And these fellows like Twy and Black Charles, could they improvise? [INTERVIEWEE] Not very much. They didn't play the style we're playing now, you see. They played mostly straight, nice trumpet but straight, you know.

ctx.x: Well, some men can improvise and some men play strictly about music, you see. Now you'll take some fellows, if you ain't got the parts there, they can't play, you see. They can't remember, you know. They can't commit anything to memory. And another guy will play a tune once, or play a spark once, and he don't need it the most. Well that's the difference, you see. But when you say a legit man is a man that, and if you've got music he'll play it, but he ain't going to put nothing to it, you see. He'll play it all…
And these fellows like Twy and Black Charles, could they improvise?
Not very much. They didn't play the style we're playing now, you see. They played mostly straight, nice trumpet but straight, you know.
